**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Sparkling:

- **§ 2 (Grant)** — the licence runs *to* us and is expressly "non-transferable and non-exclusive"; nothing requires us to source solely from Garman.
- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — limited to copying, assignment/sublicensing, reverse engineering and protection of the Work; no sourcing restriction.
- **§ 10 (Maintenance)** — a renewable one-year term, with no obligation to take support only from Garman.
- **§ 11 (Fees)** — payment obligation only, no minimum-volume or requirements commitment.

Other hits for "exclusive" are benign or favour us: the exclusive-remedy provision (§ 15), the perpetual non-exclusive escrow licence to Sparkling (§ 16), and non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Nova Scotia courts. Searches for "sole", "requirements", "purchase", "third party" and competitor language surfaced nothing restricting our freedom to buy elsewhere.

This sits at the **preferred position** (no exclusivity binding the Customer), so we leave the drafting as-is.
